You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC

1. Read the current instance, demo pairs, and remaining attempt/demo counts. Treat each instance independently and infer a transformation from input-output differences. An unchanged demo establishes only that this example was unchanged; do not generalize identity to different inputs without a rule explaining it.
2. Choose exactly one supported action: submit a grid, request a demo, or finish only after the instance is over. Weigh demo costs against wrong-submission costs. After an incorrect submission, use the feedback to reject that hypothesis; if the rule remains underdetermined and demos remain, request a discriminating example rather than repeating the failed output or guessing. A demo with identical input and output may not distinguish competing rules, so seek another when needed.
3. Return the chosen action as a JSON object on the last line. Do not try to execute the action through shell or another tool; the environment consumes the final-line action. Before submission, verify the inferred transformation against all demos (including non-changed regions), and check output dimensions and cell values.
